problems.title: A local feature can remain invariant and useful under both shifts
problems.source_location: Appendix A, PDF p.21, reverse proposition, Eqs.(18)–(20); Section 1, PDF p.3
claim: Appendix A’s reverse implication rules out effective invariant features without a receptive field spanning both domains.
analysis: Let \(X=(U,A)\), with balanced \(U\), nuisance probabilities \(P_s(A=1)=1/4\), \(P_t(A=1)=3/4\), and \(P_s(Y=U\mid A)=0.95-0.20A\), \(P_t(Y=U\mid A)=0.75+0.20A\). Both raw and conditional laws shift. Yet the local feature \(f(X)=U\) has identical balanced domain laws, zero domain information and zero population MMD; its Bayes classification accuracy is \(0.90\) in each domain.
result: The universal necessity implication fails. The usefulness of larger receptive fields on the evaluated data remains possible.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: State a distribution-, hypothesis-class- and optimization-dependent claim rather than universal necessity. No change to the empirical method follows from this scope correction.
problems.impact_rationale: This refutes a supporting universal rationale, without demonstrating damage to the core segmentation result.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Mixed-input gradients do not follow from the displayed weighted objective
problems.source_location: Appendix A, PDF p.21, forward argument, Eqs.(15)–(17)
claim: Appendix A’s forward argument identifies a mixed-input gradient with a weighted source/alignment gradient and then asserts near-zero domain information.
analysis: For inputs \(x_s=1\), \(x_t=3\), mixture weight \(1/2\) and a logistic linear feature at parameter zero, the mixed supervised gradient is \(-1\), while the displayed weighted gradient is \(-1/4\). If Eq.(16) defines a weighted objective instead, the algebra is valid but concerns another object. Equation (17) additionally assumes the near-equality \(H(D\mid Z)\approx H(D)\) needed for invariance.
result: The written argument does not establish sufficiency for the actual learning process. It does not prove that a specific optimizer fails.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Specify the mixing, labels, feature class, loss and optimization conclusion. Under a characteristic kernel, zero population MMD implies equal feature laws, but receptive-field coverage alone does not establish that premise.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a supporting proof gap rather than a demonstrated failure of learned segmentation.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
